title: Adaptive fastpath orchestrator for quantized kernels and attention prefetching
creator: Marco Chen
description: Goal: Implement an adaptive 'fastpath orchestrator' that routes requests to quantization-friendly kernels (INT8/FP8/mixed-precision) while coordinating attention prefetch and prefill/decode scheduling to amortize dequantization overhead. The orchestrator should: 1) score kernel candidates per-layer using empirical cost and quality models, 2) steer low-latency requests to minimal-dequant fastpaths when accuracy delta is acceptable, 3) trigger background prefetches for attention KV blocks for expected decode windows, and 4) fall back to higher-precision kernels when quality regressions cross thresholds. Motivation: current dequant+requant overhead spikes p95 latency for short decode windows and streaming use-cases. By combining kernel selection with attention prefetch and small-window KV reuse we expect to reduce p95 by ~20-35% on typical chat workloads while keeping avg-LLM quality loss <0.5% per our eval metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Adaptive kernel selector plumbs into runtime kernel table and makes per-request decisions based on sequence length, model variant, and latency budget
Attention prefetch module issues asynchronous KV prefetches for decode windows predicted by the decode scheduler
End-to-end p95 token latency improvement >= 15% on representative VLLM microbenchmarks (chat short-turn, 8k context, batch size 1)
Quality regression measured on production prompt-set <= 0.5% measured by Rouge-L and model entropic distance; automatic rollback policy in place
Integration tests for mixed-precision fallback, ensuring no silent corruption when switching kernel paths
Observability: per-request kernel decision and prefetch events emitted to Console traces and a perf dashboard
implementation_notes: Design choices: - Kernel scoring: combine a lightweight latency estimator (amortized dequant cost + kernel runtime samples) with a quality penalty heuristic derived from per-layer sensitivity scoring. - Fastpath criteria: sequence length < 512 and decode budget < 50ms => prefer minimal-dequant path. - Prefetch windowing: use a rolling predictor based on recent decode token intervals; prefetch predicted KV shards asynchronously with backpressure to avoid memory blowout. - Fallback: implement deterministic per-layer checks that validate output statistics (checksum + distribution drift) for early detection of precision-related corruption. - Config knobs: per-customer SLO bias, per-model quality tolerance, and max-background-prefetches. - Interaction with batching: prefetches must be shared across microbatches; kernel selector must consider aggregate batch latency and memory footprint. - This work reuses the kernel vignette from ENG-56011 (shadow kernel harness) for safe rollout and AB testing.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for kernel scoring function across synthetic latency/quality profiles. 2) Integration test harness: synthetic stream generator that emits chat-turn patterns with variable token rates to validate prefetch fairness and memory bounds. 3) Perf benchmarks on dedicated-capacity staging: p50/p95/p99 token latencies for short-turn and long-in-context workloads (1k/8k). 4) Regression suite using production prompt-set for quality checks (automated) and human spot-check for edge cases. 5) Canary rollout: start with 1% of production requests, escalate with health gates (error rate, quality deltas, latency).
risks: Incorrect prefetch predictions can increase memory and reduce throughput under high concurrency
Mixed-precision fallbacks triggered too often could negate latency wins
Quality regressions escaping automated metrics for niche prompts
Observability gaps could make incidents hard to diagnose without adding tracing events upfront
